ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, and the points $D$, $E$, $F$ are on the sides $BC$, $AB$, $AC$, respectively, with $CD=BE$ and $BD=CF$. If $\angle EDF = 42^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=AC$, \\
it follows that $\angle B=\angle C$, \\
In $\triangle BDE$ and $\triangle CFD$, \\
$\begin{cases}
BD=CF\\
\angle B=\angle C\\
BE=CD
\end{cases}$, \\
hence, $\triangle BDE \cong \triangle CFD$, \\
therefore, $\angle EDB=\angle DFC$, $\angle FDC=\angle BED$, \\
since $\angle EDF+\angle BDE+\angle FDC=180^\circ$, $\angle B+\angle BED+\angle EDB=180^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle B=\angle EDF=42^\circ$, \\
thus, $\angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=\boxed{96^\circ}$.

令c=cosβ，s=sinβ。则向量DE=E-D=(c-t(1+c),(1-t)s)，向量DF=F-D=(1-t(1+c),ts)。计算长度平方：|DE|^2=[c-t(1+c)]^2+[(1-t)s]^2=1-2t(1-t)(1+c)，同样|DF|^2=[1-t(1+c)]^2+(ts)^2=1-2t(1-t)(1+c)。再算点积：DE·DF=[c-t(1+c)][1-t(1+c)]+t(1-t)s^2=c[1-2t(1-t)(1+c)]。因此cos∠EDF=(DE·DF)/(|DE||DF|)=c=cosβ。由于β是三角形底角，∠EDF=β。已知∠EDF=42°，所以β=42°。于是∠BAC=180°-2β=180°-84°=96°。

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$. Points $D$, $E$, and $F$ lie on sides $BC$, $AB$, and $AC$, respectively, with $CD=BE$ and $BD=CF$. If $\angle EDF = 42^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BAC$?
raw_record.answer: Since $AB=AC$, it follows that $\angle B=\angle C$. In $\triangle BDE$ and $\triangle CFD$, $BD=CF$, $\angle B=\angle C$, and $BE=CD$, hence $\triangle BDE \cong \triangle CFD$. Therefore, $\angle EDB=\angle DFC$ and $\angle FDC=\angle BED$. Since $\angle EDF+\angle BDE+\angle FDC=180^\circ$ and $\angle B+\angle BED+\angle EDB=180^\circ$, it follows that $\angle B=\angle EDF=42^\circ$. Thus, $\angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=\boxed{96^\circ}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: Both attached figures show the same geometric structure: In triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the base; D is located on the base BC; E is located on side AB; F is located on side AC; segments ED and FD are drawn, forming angle EDF. Reasoning: From the given condition AB=AC, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, so the base angles are equal, namely ∠B=∠C. Compare triangles BDE and CFD: The given conditions provide BD=CF and BE=CD; also, since DB is on BC and BE is on BA, ∠DBE=∠B; at the same time, FC is on CA and CD is on CB, so ∠FCD=∠C. Since ∠B=∠C, therefore ∠DBE=∠FCD. Thus triangles BDE and CFD are congruent by SAS. From corresponding angles of congruent triangles being equal, obtain ∠BDE=∠DFC, and ∠FDC=∠BED. Because B, D, C are collinear, the three angles above point D satisfy ∠BDE+∠EDF+∠FDC=180°. And in triangle BDE, ∠B+∠BED+∠BDE=180°. After substituting ∠FDC=∠BED, comparing the two equations gives ∠EDF=∠B. It is known that ∠EDF=42°, so ∠B=42°. Also ∠B=∠C, so ∠C=42°. Therefore ∠BAC=180°-42°-42°=96°.
